title.narrative: Envelopes 1 2: Provision of Life‐saving assistance to ensure emergency services to the most vulnerable IDPs in Northwest Syria through integrated multisectoral ESNFI and Protection/GBV activities

description.narrative:
ESNFI
This integrated multi-sectoral project will target 250 HHs (30 HHs will benefit from cash for dignified shelter units establishment, and 220 HHs will benefit from cash for light shelter rehabilitation) in Balion Alothman camp in Torlaha community in Harim district through providing Cash for Shelter (self-help modality) is an implementation modality that effectively helps vulnerable households meet their immediate needs in a dignified way that reinforces community resilience. Through Cash for shelter intervention, IYD transfers conditional cash allowances directly to selected vulnerable households in order to support them in meeting their basic need for shelter rehabilitation. In addition, participants receiving Cash for Shelter also benefit from the necessary and tailored technical support of IYD's Shelter Team.
The displaced HHs in the targeted camp are currently living in poor shelter units condition they are mainly made from bricks with plastic roofs, and the shelter units lack necessary items to resist the winter conditions, such as cracks in walls and roofs, essential facilities for elderly and PWDs, additionally there are 30 HHs (out of total 250 HHs living in the camp) in the targeted camp they are still living in tents so those HHs will be targeted by cash for dignified shelter units establishment.
Shelter repairs and rehabilitation are implemented through Cash for Shelter, targeting 250 houses in Bailon Alothman where the IDPs live in their damaged Shelter units and damaged tents. The Cash is transferred in three rounds to the selected participants through financial service providers and following IYD's cash standard operating procedures: - 40% of the grant amount is transferred at the beginning of the rehabilitation works, - 30% is transferred when rehabilitation reaches 50% based on the supervision team estimation and following the progress reported - 30% after completion of certificate realized. The project will be implemented through six main steps in Balion Alothman camp as follows: 1. beneficiaries' selection 2. Market assessment 3. Household and shelter identification and assessments 4. conduct the cash distribution for shelter rehabilitation 5. implementation and quality assurance 6. Monitoring
As for Cash for winter activity, the project will target 1973 HHs living in the targeted camps (attached) each HH will receive 150 USD. Protection/GBV Under envelope 1, and in the same target locations of ESNFI, we seek to increase the protection and resilience of affected individuals by improving access to GBV prevention, response, and empowerment interventions in and around seven (6) widow camps in Dana, Salqin, and Armanza sub-districts, Harim, Idleb. (GBV SC confirmation). GBV activities will be conducted inside 2 WGSSs to be established inside 2 widow camps to provide GBV services inside and around 6 proposed widows camps. Services: case management linked with case funds, PSS, AMAL initiative (YMC), vocational training, and IGA/small grants inside WGSSs, awareness raising\info sessions, SIR, safety audit, and the establishment and training of 6 women’s committees. GBV field staff consists of 2/ WGSS assistants, 2/GBV field supervisors, 4 case managers, 10/social workers (6: F, 4:M), and 4 PSS workers MampE activities will be in line with the MampE toolkit and IYD MampE policy (attached). A special referral of FHHs in and around widows’ camps to the IYD SNFI team to receive winterization assistance is explained above.
